profiles.title: All Saints
profiles.subject: Saints

overview.text: The Orthodox Church in America dedicates the Sunday following Pentecost to all saints, including those known only to God. Its account includes apostles, martyrs, prophets, hierarchs, monastics, and righteous people, joining diverse lives through the work of the Holy Spirit.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: The selected Russian icon, dated 1890, assembles many ranks of haloed saints below a heavenly register. The file description identifies the subject as All Saints. This particular historical composition represents a collective gathering rather than a portrait of one named saint.

sourceRefs.locator: File description and displayed historic reproduction

blocks.text: The OCA account cautiously proposes that the feast may have begun as a commemoration of all martyrs and later widened. It also describes the feast’s prominence in the reign of Emperor Leo VI and his wife, Empress Theophano, in the ninth century.

blocks.text: The same account distinguishes confessors from executed martyrs: confessors suffered for their faith without being put to death. It also includes righteous people who attained holiness while living in ordinary society. The categories describe different forms of witness, not one required biography.
